scope: Read saved public/synthetic evaluation rows only. Classification does not establish causal engine internals and does not upgrade alternate orthography to exact success. No input/ranking/timing changes.

classification_rules.primary_miss: Exact frozen text rank is null or greater than9 in fresh ordinary compact plain Yale.
classification_rules.diagnostic_rescue: Same exact text reaches first9 under saved diagnostic input. Tones/apostrophes are separate requests, never a primary-input success.
classification_rules.wrong_initial: Report both rank1 initial-character mismatch and absence of exact first character among all first9; neither alone proves the root cause.
classification_rules.near_variant_rule: Same entire string only after explicit character-group normalization. Strict orthography and colloquial written variants are labeled separately. This is a report-only surface annotation, not linguistic interchangeability or primary exact success.
classification_rules.closest_saved_candidate: Levenshtein character edit distance among saved first9; ties choose the earlier saved rank.
classification_rules.dictionary_support: Copied exact lexical-support metadata from the frozen fixture-validation report. No database or candidate queries were run.

systemic_followups.area: Tone-free sequence ranking and search coverage
systemic_followups.evidence: 18 of23 first9 misses become exact first9 hits with tone digits; six exact plain-Yale targets are absent first90. Target prefixes often survive while the rest becomes competing dictionary words.
systemic_followups.proposal: Investigate context/word-transition scoring and candidate-budget diversity over complete paths. Test against fixed authored and external cases; do not inject case-specific phrases or change gold after inspection.

systemic_followups.area: Habitual ng versus true syllabic ng
systemic_followups.evidence: 0 of29 habitual-ng exact targets appear first90 fresh; short/heavy synthetic histories reach17/16 first9 and23/23 first90, still below policy.
systemic_followups.proposal: Make the user-requested ng-for-唔 input behavior an explicit, bounded and reviewable policy, preserving genuine ng/m readings and separating alias support from learned ranking. Re-evaluate with fresh and varied synthetic histories.

systemic_followups.evidence: Some exact misses have a near-written variant in first9, including 麵/面 and 哋/地 or 吓/下. Others are genuine competing words and cannot be dismissed as typography.
systemic_followups.proposal: Consider explicit output-spelling preference and context-sensitive written-form ranking. Keep the current exact targets and primary failure counts unchanged; evaluate any future alternate-output policy separately.

systemic_followups.area: Do not substitute manual boundaries for the requested workflow
systemic_followups.evidence: Only one of23 plain-Yale first9 misses is rescued by adding all syllable apostrophes.
systemic_followups.proposal: Preserve apostrophes as an optional diagnostic/control, while improving the ordinary compact-input experience rather than requiring users to delimit every syllable.

release_recommendation: Withhold new installation/publication. The predeclared authored quality gates fail; saved synthetically learned improvements do not establish confidence for ordinary long-phrase use. Timing and external replay are separate reports.
